limitations: The 1636 roll is a single household-scaled allocation, not a Weymouth census; the absence bounds his householder standing in 1636, not necessarily his physical presence in the town.
Two of his later East Field abutters, Edmund Hart and Thomas Rawling, do appear in the 1636 cohort, so the East Field itself was being settled by 1636.

outgoing.explanation: The 1636 householder absence is a cross-topic lower edge on the arrival window developed in the arrival-chronology unit (arrival after 1636).
The 1636 great-lot absence refines the start of John's inhabitant standing: he was not yet a Weymouth householder in 1636, so his admitted-inhabitant window opens after 1636.
